snippets.output: A 36-year-old man with minimal improvement after 2 months of citalopram has not shown an adequate response to citalopram, so the most appropriate next step in management is to switch to a different antidepressant.
Studies have shown that switching to a different antidepressant after an inadequate response to initial treatment can be beneficial.
Switching to a different antidepressant is a reasonable next step for the 36-year-old man because the 36-year-old man has not experienced a full response to citalopram after 2 months.

Amitriptyline is a tricyclic antidepressant that may be considered as a second-line treatment for a 36-year-old man with depression and minimal improvement after 2 months of citalopram, but it carries a higher risk of side effects, particularly anticholinergic effects.
Mirtazapine may be considered as an adjunct to citalopram in a 36-year-old man with depression who has had minimal improvement after 2 months of citalopram therapy.
In a 36-year-old man with depression who has had minimal improvement after 2 months of citalopram, adding another medication may increase the risk of adverse effects.

Electroconvulsive therapy may be considered if symptoms are severe or if there is a high risk of suicide; in this 36-year-old man with depression after 2 months of citalopram, the symptoms are not severe and there is no high risk of suicide.
Switching a 36-year-old man from citalopram to paroxetine is not indicated because citalopram and paroxetine are both SSRIs.

Phenelzine is a monoamine oxidase inhibitor that requires strict dietary restriction and lifestyle modification, making phenelzine a less practical choice for a 36-year-old man with depression who has had minimal improvement after 2 months of citalopram.
For a 36-year-old man with depression who has had minimal improvement after 2 months of citalopram therapy, switching to nortriptyline is the most appropriate next step in management.
Nortriptyline has been shown to be effective in patients with inadequate response to an initial treatment.
